zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Infiṭār
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾, that is: "split open". The heaven will split open on the Day of Resurrection with the clouds, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said.
«[Translator's note: the source quotes no verse after "as He said".]»

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَإذا الكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ﴾, that is: they fell down and dropped one after another.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا البِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ﴾: the sweet water burst forth into the salt.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإذا القُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾: he means «بُحْثِرَتْ», that is: their earth is turned over and the dead in them are resurrected.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وأخَّرَتْ﴾: what it sent ahead of the deeds it was commanded to do, and what it held back of them and did not do. It was also said: «وَأخَّرَتْ» means: whatever practice (sunna) it instituted that was acted upon after it.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الإنْسانُ ما غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الكَرِيمِ﴾, that is: what deceived you and enticed you until you neglected what was obligatory upon you?!

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ﴾, that is: He created you in the best stature. It is read «فَعَدَّلَكَ» both without doubling and with doubling.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿فِي أيِّ صُورَةٍ ما شاءَ رَكَّبَكَ﴾: «ما» may be an emphasising connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant), and the meaning is: "in whatever form He willed He assembled you — whether tall or short, whether handsome or otherwise." And «ما» may be in the sense of condition and requital (sharṭ wa-jazāʾ), so that the meaning is: "in whatever form He wills to assemble you in, He assembles you."

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ﴾, that is: rather, you deny that you will be resurrected and judged, that is, requited for your deeds. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, informed them that their deeds are preserved, saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 12], so they write it down against them.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾: the Day of Requital, which is the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:17-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ ما أدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾: He repeated the mention of the day to magnify its importance.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ — it was also read «يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ». Whoever read it in the nominative did so on the basis that the "day" is an attribute (ṣifa) of His saying «يَوْمُ الدِّينِ». It may also be nominative with «هُوَ» implied, so that the meaning is: "it is a day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul." It may also be in the position of the nominative while being indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, because it is annexed to His saying «لا تَمْلِكُ»; for what is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr al-mutamakkin) may be made indeclinable on the fatḥa, even though it is in the position of a nominative or a genitive, as the poet said:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing kept her from drinking except that a dove cooed among branches laden with fruit.)
— he annexed «غَيْرَ» to «أنْ نَطَقَتْ» and so made it indeclinable on the fatḥa. And its accusative may be according to the meaning of these things mentioned: it is ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾.
«[Translator's note: the source text ends here; the explanation of the accusative appears to be incomplete.]»
